title: Visitor from the Shadows
next_chapter_hook: Chen Ji embarks on the path to the Imperial Capital, unaware that his blood brother Chen Tianming has been laying out a strategy in the royal city for a millennium—this encounter between siblings who have never met will unleash a storm of blood and carnage.

text.content:
In the corner of the ruined temple, Chen Ji sat cross-legged, spiritual energy slowly circulating around him. After three days of feigning death, he had hidden in this desolate place, using the broken shelter to heal his injuries and nurture his qi. The aura of the Tianji Record had been weakening over these three days, yet it refused to disappear completely—this was both his greatest hidden danger and a predicament he had to face. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul flickered faintly within the depths of the Tianji Record, as if contemplating something.

"In three days, there will be a variable." After speaking these words, Mo Xiansheng fell into silence, refusing to say more no matter how Chen Ji pressed him.

Variable—what could it be? Chen Ji's brow furrowed slightly. He had been scheming for years, leaving nothing to chance, from sect internal strife to demonic path invasions, from Ling Yuan's ambushes to the Heavenly Eye's surveillance. Every step had been within his calculations. But these three days of waiting filled him with an unprecedented restlessness—as if something was slipping beyond his control.

Outside the ruined temple, the night wind howled mournfully.

Just as Chen Ji was about to enter meditation again, a voice suddenly sounded in his ear: "You're here."

The voice was soft, yet it exploded like thunder in Chen Ji's Mental Sea. His pupils contracted sharply, every hair on his body standing on end—with his keen spiritual awareness, he had not detected anyone approaching at all! This realization made cold sweat instantly break out on Chen Ji's back.

He opened his eyes abruptly, his palm already gathering a blade of sharp spiritual energy, his voice cold as the frigid wind of the Nine Netherworlds: "Who goes there?!"

Before the words finished, Chen Ji had already risen, surveying his surroundings. Yet the ruined temple was empty, with only the broken deity statue casting eerie shadows under the moonlight, no figure visible anywhere. But that voice spoke again, this time right beside him, as if whispering at his ear:

"Don't be impatient, Ji'er."

dialogue.content:
Ji'er?

These two words were like a thunderbolt, cleaving all thoughts in Chen Ji's mind. His body froze in place, even forgetting to breathe.

This form of address... this was something only blood relatives would use...

Chen Ji suppressed the turbulent waves in his heart, his voice extremely low yet carrying a dangerous chill: "Playing tricks? If you truly are an ancestor of the Chen Family, why not reveal yourself?"

The moment his words fell, within the shadows of the ruined temple, a illusory figure slowly took shape. That figure was ancient and majestic, surrounded by faint spiritual light; though merely a wisp of remnant soul, it radiated a terrifying pressure.

The instant Chen Ji saw that face, his pupils contracted again—it was the ancestral portrait enshrined in the Chen Family shrine!

The ancestor's illusory form nodded slightly, his voice aged and profound: "A thousand years of preparation, merely to await a destined one capable of inheriting the Tianji Record. Ji'er, you have exceeded my expectations."

Chen Ji was not moved by these words; his gaze remained cold as a blade: "Ancestor? The Chen Family ancestors all achieved nirvana a thousand years ago—how could there be remnant souls persisting until now?"

He paused, his tone gaining more sarcasm: "Moreover, even if you truly are an ancestor, after a thousand years of separation, appearing now to speak such words—do you wish for your grandson to be moved to tears and obediently hand over the Tianji Record?"

The ancestor's illusory form seemed unconcerned with Chen Ji's sarcasm, instead revealing a satisfied smile: "As I anticipated, your nature is resolute and you do not trust easily. This is good."

Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul fluctuated intensely within the depths of the Tianji Record, as if sensing something, yet he did not speak.

text.content:
Chen Ji coldly watched the ancestor's illusory form, while his mind raced calculations. He could sense that this illusory form before him possessed unfathomable strength—even in its remnant soul state, it was not something he could currently contend with. But precisely for this reason, he grew even more wary—why would such a powerful being appear now? Why seek out this "waste" like himself?

"Since the ancestor speaks of a thousand-year scheme," Chen Ji spoke, his voice calm, "then surely you should know that the Tianji Record choosing me was not my own desire. How much do you know of the Heavenly Eye, the fall of prophets through the ages, and Ling Yuan's ambushes?"

The ancestor's illusory form slowly shook his head; those deep eyes seemed capable of seeing through all illusions: "Ji'er, when do you think the Heavenly Eye's chess game began?"

Chen Ji's brow furrowed: "Could it not be from ancient times?"

The ancestor let out a low laugh, one carrying a hint of bitterness and helplessness: "Ancient times? No. Ji'er, the Heavenly Eye's chess game has from the very beginning been a continuation of the Chen Family's internal strife."

dialogue.content:
Hearing these words, Chen Ji's mind was shaken to its core.

Chen Family internal strife? The Heavenly Eye was a continuation of Chen Family internal strife?

He forced himself to remain calm, his voice still steady: "What does the ancestor mean by this?"

The ancestor's illusory form paced slowly, his voice aged and heavy: "A thousand years ago, my twin brother and I competed for the inheritance right of the Tianji Record. I won; he lost. But he refused to accept defeat, using a secret technique to merge a wisp of his spiritual consciousness into the heavens, assuming the identity of Heavenly Will to lay out this thousand-year chess game—"

"The ancestor means to say that the Heavenly Eye is actually the twin brother of the Chen Family's ancestor?" Chen Ji's voice trembled slightly—not from fear, but from disbelief.

The ancestor nodded: "He uses the name of heaven to carry out revenge. Every successor of the Tianji Record has been his chess piece—including you."

text.content:
Chen Ji fell silent.

He had believed himself to be flawless in strategy, believed himself to be secretly manipulating the world, yet he had never realized that from the beginning, he was merely a piece on someone else's chessboard. The Heavenly Eye's game was not some grand foresight of the Heavenly Will, but merely a continuation of an old grudge within the Chen Family.

What did this mean? It meant that Ling Yuan's pursuit, the demonic path's invasion, the secrets of the royal city—all might merely be the chess game laid by the Chen Family ancestor's twin brother. And he, Chen Ji, was nothing more than a chess piece pushed forward by fate.

Chen Ji's fists slowly clenched, his knuckles turning white.

Yet in the next moment, the rage in his eyes was gradually replaced by calm calculation. He raised his head, his gaze sharp as a blade striking toward the ancestor's illusory form: "The ancestor choosing to appear at this moment—surely it wasn't merely to tell your grandson these things?"

The ancestor smiled faintly, seemingly very satisfied with Chen Ji's reaction: "Of course not."

dialogue.content:
The ancestor's illusory form raised his hand and waved, and a illusory map unfolded before Chen Ji. It was the layout of the royal city, with dense lines marking various important locations, and at the map's very center—the location of the Imperial Palace Dragon Vein—a point of light flickered.

"The complete Tianji Record contains nine pages; you currently possess only three." The ancestor's voice was calm. "The seventh page lies hidden within the core of this royal city's Dragon Vein."

Chen Ji's gaze shifted slightly: "The royal city's Dragon Vein? That is the forbidden grounds of the Great Yan Dynasty—even approaching is impossible for ordinary people."

The ancestor nodded: "Correct. The Heavenly Eye chose that location precisely because the Dragon Vein could provide sufficient power to sustain his chess game. But equally, it is also the key to breaking the game."

Chen Ji did not speak, merely watching the ancestor silently.

"Do you wish to know why?" the ancestor asked.

Chen Ji shook his head: "Since the ancestor speaks of a thousand-year scheme, surely you long anticipated this day. Whatever choice I make, it was likely all within the ancestor's calculations."

text.content:
The ancestor's illusory form smiled again, and this time, that smile carried a complex mix of emotions: "Ji'er, you are wrong. My thousand-year scheme was not to make you walk my path, but to give you a chance to choose."

He paused briefly; the illusory form began to grow even more faint: "I thought you would choose to continue hiding. After all, given your nature, that would be the most prudent path. But I did not anticipate—your brother would become the greatest variable in this chess game."

Chen Ji was stunned: "Brother?"

He had never heard of having a brother.

The ancestor nodded; the illusory form grew increasingly faint, yet his voice remained clear: "Your twin brother, Chen Tianming. Not only is he still alive—"

Chen Ji's breath stopped abruptly.

"But he is within the royal city." The ancestor finally said, "He is the one chosen by the Heavenly Eye, your greatest opponent in this lifetime, and the only one who can help you break the chess game."

With these words, the ancestor's illusory form completely dissolved, leaving only a faint spiritual fluctuation lingering in the air.

Chen Ji stood alone in the ruined temple, speechless for a long while.

In his mind, the ancestor's words echoed continuously, exploding like thunder. Chen Tianming—this name he had never heard before now pierced his heart like a sharp blade.

Brother. He actually still had a brother.

Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, forcibly suppressing the turbulent waves in his heart. His face appeared especially pallid in the moonlight, yet those eyes gradually regained their usual depth and composure.

"Chen Tianming..." he murmured this name quietly, a meaningful curve forming at the corner of his mouth, "Interesting."

Outside the ruined temple, the night wind howled. In the direction of the Tianqing Sect, spiritual fluctuations could be faintly detected—Ling Yuan was laying a net of heaven and earth to search. And in the farther direction of the royal city, there was only dead silence, as if something was lurking in the darkness, awaiting his arrival.

text.content:
Chen Ji opened his eyes, a decisive light flashing within them. Since fate had given him this opportunity, he had no reason to retreat.

"Ancestor," he said quietly, his voice echoing in the empty ruined temple, "Since you said this is a choice, then I choose—I want to personally see what manner of being this brother of mine truly is."

The moment these words fell, a warm current surged from the depths of his Mental Sea—that was the final gift left by the ancestor's remnant soul. Spiritual energy flowed through his meridians, repairing his damaged body while also awakening the Tianji Record's dormant potential that had long been sleeping.

text.content:
Chen Ji was silent for a moment, then ultimately shook his head.

"What the ancestor said sounds reasonable, but who knows if it's another trap?" His voice was low. "Chen Tianming... I've never heard this name before. Suddenly appearing and claiming to be my brother—it's too suspicious."

He sat back down cross-legged, deciding to continue his original plan—to wait for Ling Yuan to reveal a weakness, then seize the opportunity to act.

text.content:
Chen Ji did not rise immediately. Instead, he dove his divine consciousness deep into the Mental Sea, confronting the remnant soul directly.

"Mo Xiansheng," his voice was calm yet carried an undeniable pressure, "when the Ancestor appeared, why did you not say a word? How much do you know about this name—Chen Tianming?"

Mo Xiansheng remained silent for a long while before finally sighing: "Ji'er, some things... the timing isn't right. I cannot say."

Chen Jisneereded coldly: "Timing again? In your words, is this 'timing' for my sake, or for your own?"

Mo Xiansheng fell silent once more. The broken figure within the depths of the Tianji Record trembled faintly.

Chen Ji did not press further. He knew Mo Xiansheng too well. This existence that guarded the Tianji Record in remnant soul form—every word he spoke was calculation, and every silence was also calculation. He never believed Mo Xiansheng would help him unconditionally—just as he never believed anyone would help him unconditionally.

Outside the dilapidated temple, the night wind began to rise.

Chen Ji stood up and walked to the temple's entrance, gazing at the dark horizon in the distance. The Ancestor's words still echoed in his mind, each word like a blade, cutting through his自以为是的认知—his illusion of understanding.

Chen Family's internal strife. Heavenly Eye. Chen Tianming.

He thought he had laid out a game of chess spanning the world, only to discover he was merely a corner piece on someone else's board. He thought he was the chess player, only to realize he had been a chess piece from the very beginning.

But so what?

A cold smile slowly curved Chen Ji's lips, while deep in his eyes, a dangerous gleam flickered.

dialogue.content:
"Even a chess piece has the day it can overturn the chessboard."

Chen Ji said in a low voice, his words scattered by the night wind, yet carrying an undeniable resolve.

He turned around and glanced one final time at the broken deity statue inside the temple. The statue's features were already blurred, appearing especially eerie under the moonlight. Yet Chen Ji felt as if the statue was watching him, wearing some kind of profound smile.

"Chen Tianming..." He murmured this name, his cold aura growing increasingly intense, "regardless of whether you are enemy or ally, since the Ancestor said you can break the chess game, then I'll go see for myself—what本事 does this chess piece possess."

He strode out of the temple, the night wind billowing his robes. His silhouette quickly vanished into the night, leaving only a trail of faint footprints behind.

text.content:
At the moment Chen Ji departed, deep within the imperial capital far away, a pair of eyes slowly opened.

They were eyes extremely similar to Chen Ji's—deep, cold, as if capable of seeing through all falsehood in the world. The owner of these eyes sat in a luxurious palace, surrounded by faint dragon energy, the aura of the imperial city's dragon vein.

"Brother, so you're finally coming?"

The man murmured softly, his voice carrying an indescribably complex emotion. Before him, an illusory chessboard slowly materialized, with black and white pieces interlaced across its surface, and at the very center, two pieces were slowly drawing closer.

One was Chen Ji.

The other was him—Chen Tianming.

Chen Tianming's lips curved into a smile, a smile containing three parts anticipation, three parts wariness, three parts calculation, and one part emotion even he himself could not name.

"A thousand-year layout, and finally the endgame approaches." He said softly, "Brother, don't disappoint me."

Meanwhile, in the secret chamber deep within the Tianqing Sect.

The old Sect Master sat in the main seat, his aged face appearing especially gloomy under the candlelight. Before him, a Jade Slip glowed faintly—it was a magical artifact that tracked Chen Ji's feigned death aura.

"Still not dead?" Ling Yuan冷声哼道, his withered fingers gently tapping the Jade Slip, "Sure enough, a bane that lingers for a thousand years."

A狠厉 flash crossed his eyes: "Since not dead, then kill him again."

The moment his voice fell, several black shadows surged from the darkness, kneeling on one knee, awaiting orders.

Ling Yuan's voice was icy as the cold wind of the Nine Netherworlds: "Transmit the order—seal off a thousand li around the Tianqing Sect. Before he reaches the imperial capital, bring back Chen Ji's head."

"Yes!"

The shadows dissolved into darkness once more, vanishing without a trace.

Ling Yuan sat alone in the secret chamber, gazing at the night sky beyond the window, a grim smile curling at the corner of his lips.

"Chen Ji啊 Chen Ji, you thought fake death could save you from disaster? How naive."

Night wrapped the entire land like ink.

Chen Ji hastened across the wilderness, his form gliding like a ghost. In his mind, the Ancestor's words constantly reverberated, interweaving with his own plans, forming a completely new chess game.

Imperial Capital. Chen Tianming. The Seventh Page of the Tianji Record.

And Ling Yuan's pursuit.

He knew he had stepped onto the most dangerous path, yet he had no choice. The Ancestor's words had revealed a shocking truth—the Heavenly Eye's chess game was actually a continuation of the Chen Family's internal strife a thousand years ago. And his encounter with Chen Tianming would determine the final outcome of this millennium-spanning grudge.

"Chen Tianming..." Chen Jiwhispered念着 this name, his cold aura growing increasingly intense, "regardless of whether you're enemy or ally, in this game, I will not lose."

His silhouette vanished into the night, leaving only a sentence echoing in the wind:

"Because I, Chen Ji, have never been a piece to be manipulated."

The wheel of fate turned once more, and this time, Chen Ji was determined to become the chess player.
